title: Up 50%, Down 50%
objective: After this level you can explain why a 50% drop followed by a 50% rise leaves you worse off than where you began.
summary: A 50% fall and a 50% rise leave you 25% below where you began, in either order, because each percent is taken from a different starting value. Recovering from a 50% fall takes a 100% rise.

cards.headline: Your $100 drops 50%, then rises 50%. Back to $100, right?
cards.body: Nope. You end up with $75. No fees, no tricks, just arithmetic. Here's where the missing $25 went.

cards.headline: Each percent has its own starting point
cards.body: The first 50% is taken from $100, so you lose $50 and have $50 left. The second 50% is measured from that new, smaller start: half of $50 is only $25. Up $25 lands you at $75. Same percent, different base, so the fall and the rise aren't the same size in dollars. It's Level 3's "up from what?" twice in a row.

cards.headline: The order doesn't save you
cards.body: Flip it. Up 50% first: $100 becomes $150. Then down 50%: half of $150 is $75 gone, leaving $75 again. Whenever a rise and a fall of the same percent follow each other, the second one works on a different number, and you finish below the start. Even up 10% then down 10% turns $100 into $99.

cards.fact: After a 50% fall, you need a 100% rise to get back.
cards.context: From $50, climbing back to $100 means gaining another $50, and 50 ÷ 50 is 1, or 100%. The deeper the fall, the steeper the climb back. So when something "fell 50% and has bounced back 50%", you know it's still a quarter below where it started.

cards.headline: Up and down: balanced?
learned: Each percent has its own base
Back from a 50% fall takes a 100% rise

questions.prompt: $100 falls 50%, then rises 50%, and ends up at _____.

options.rationale: That's after the fall; the rise adds $25 back.
The rise is taken from $50, so it only adds $25.
The rise and fall together leave you below $100, not above.

questions.explanation: Down 50% from $100 is $50; up 50% from $50 adds $25, making $75.

questions.prompt: Your $100 drops 50%, then rises 50%. Put the amounts in order, from start to finish.
questions.explanation: You start with $100. Losing 50% leaves $50, and a 50% rise on $50 adds only $25, so you finish at $75.

questions.prompt: Using Level 3's rule (change ÷ start), what rise takes $50 back to $100?
questions.explanation: The change is $50 and the start is $50: 50 ÷ 50 = 1, a 100% rise.
